mandatory_rules: Group all logs that share the exact same Process ID (PID) into a single, foundational 'Event Core'. This grouping is absolute for activities within a single process lifecycle and these cores must not be split.

If a unique, high-cardinality session or transaction identifier is present across multiple logs (potentially with different PIDs), group them into a single 'Event Core'. This rule takes precedence over PID grouping for tracking distributed transactions.
heuristic_rules: **[MERGE EVENT CORES Rule for SSH Brute-Force/Scanning]** After initial grouping by PID, identify all 'Event Cores' from the 'sshd' process containing authentication failure templates (e.g., 'Failed password for *', 'Invalid user * from *', 'pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure'). If multiple such cores share the exact same Key Source Identifier (the source 'ip' or 'rhost' value) and their timestamps are within a defined time window (e.g., 30 minutes), merge them into a single logical 'SSH Brute-Force Attempt' event. This reconstructs the full attack campaign from a single actor across multiple spawned processes.

**[KEY DIMENSION SPLIT Rule]** Even if logs are temporally adjacent, if they represent external interactions and their Key Source Identifier (e.g., the 'ip' or 'rhost' field) changes, the corresponding Event Cores MUST start new, separate logical events. Each unique source IP represents a distinct actor and context.

**[BOUNDARY Rule by State Change - Success]** An Event Core containing the template 'Accepted password for <*> from <*>' signifies a successful login. This core MUST start a new 'Successful SSH Session' event and must NOT be merged with any preceding failure-based events, even if they share the same Key Source Identifier and occur within the time window.

**[STATE TRANSITION BOUNDARY Rule - Session End]** An Event Core containing the template 'pam_unix(sshd:session): session closed for user <*>' marks the definitive end of a 'Successful SSH Session' event associated with that session's original PID. Any subsequent logs, even from the same user or IP, must initiate a new event.

**[MERGE & CLASSIFY Rule for Lockout]** An Event Core containing the template 'Disconnecting: Too many authentication failures for <*> [preauth]' acts as a trigger. Merge any logs from the same PID with related templates like 'message repeated <*> times...' and 'PAM <*> more authentication failures...' into a single, high-severity 'SSH Lockout Event'.

**[MERGE & CLASSIFY Rule for Connection Errors]** An Event Core containing the sequence of templates 'Bad packet length <*>. [preauth]' followed by 'Disconnecting: Packet corrupt [preauth]' should be defined as a single, complete 'Malformed SSH Packet' event. Similarly, group logs with templates like 'fatal: Read from socket failed...' or 'fatal: Write failed...' by their shared PID to form 'Abrupt Disconnect' events.

**[MERGE & CLASSIFY Rule for DNS Mismatch]** An Event Core containing the template 'Address <*> maps to <*> but this does not map back to the address - POSSIBLE BREAK-IN ATTEMPT!' should be defined as a single 'SSH DNS Mismatch Warning' event. Merge any subsequent disconnect logs from the same PID into this event.

**[TIME-BASED BOUNDARY Rule - Inactivity Timeout]** When merging multiple Event Cores into a larger logical event (such as a brute-force attack), if the time between the last log of the current event and a new candidate log from the same Key Source Identifier exceeds a specified threshold (e.g., 30 minutes), terminate the current event and begin a new one. This prevents grouping distinct, temporally separate attack waves.
